verdicts.citation: SPEC 2.6, row 'Highest root θ: the root population of largest form value that no mutation raises | unique [V]'; SPEC 2.7 F13 ('On B, C, F, G the play ends at the highest root when i is a long node and at the highest short root when i is a short node'); SPEC 4 T2 and 2.16 limit the Hasse-diagram claim to 'a simply laced board of finite type'; oracle lie_games.highest_short_root (its docstring says a finite board has one dominant positive root when simply laced and two otherwise); golden kostant.B2.end_from_node = [[1,2],[1,1]]. All of these support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6: glossary.mdx:319, row 35: 'On a board of finite type, the root population at which no mutation raises any city.' Row 36 (:327): 'The positive root populations of a board, arranged by total population, with an edge from one to another wherever a mutation raises a city.' Its Lie theory column is 'root poset'. Neither row comes from Appendix C, which has no row for either term. P6-A8 added them (decisions/P6-A8.md, 'new glossary anchors'). M1 beat 3 on the site gives the definition only in the context of E8, and M1 beat 4 limits the root poset to 'a board of finite type with single roads'. Oracle (python3 -I on copies of reference/ taken from the gate commit, positions): the positive roots p with every entry of dynkin_labels(C,p) >= 0 are B2 [(1,1),(1,2)], B3 [(1,1,1),(1,2,2)], C3 [(1,2,1),(2,2,1)], F4 [(1,2,3,2),(2,3,4,2)] and G2 [(2,1),(3,2)], against one each on A3 and D4. The form values are 2 and 4 (6 on G2). highest_root and highest_short_root return the larger and the smaller of each pair. Raising edges on B2 with L.mutate: (0,1)->(1,1) rise 1 and (1,0)->(1,2) rise 2. The root-poset covers are (0,1)<(1,1), (1,0)<(1,1) and (1,1)<(1,2). On G2 there is the edge (0,1)->(3,1) with rise 3. All of this equals the finding's observed. golden kostant.B2.end_from_node = [[1,2],[1,1]], so there are two ends, both raised by no mutation. No [D] covers the rows. No MERGE ruling, P6-A8 entry or known-and-decided item addresses them. reports/gate-G6.md names gate commit f07eec6 and records no open item on the glossary's definitions. No earlier phase 6 round exists.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because no passage permits the definition; 2.6 adds 'of largest form value' and T2 and 2.16 confine the poset claim to simply laced boards. R2 failed, because the finding reads 2.6, F13 and T2 correctly and the row itself says 'On a board of finite type'. R3 failed, because the rows are P6-A8's phase 6 completion, at gate G6. R4 failed, because the oracle (highest_short_root, golden kostant end_from_node) confirms two dominant roots on B, C, F, G and the non-Hasse raising edges. R5 failed: there is no [D] and no recorded decision. R6 failed: there is no record. The severity stays blocker, since a mathematical definition that is wrong on 16 of the 32 types is a mathematical statement presented as fact that is wrong.

verdicts.citation: SOURCES.md [DE08] ('Theorem 2.1: a connected integer-weighted graph has a terminating game from some nonzero dominant start exactly when it is a Dynkin diagram of finite type'); SPEC 2.1 ('Both games can be played on a one-way board ... but none of the theory of this section applies to it'); oracle classify and play on [[2,0],[-1,2]]; golden one_way_counterexample.cartan = [[2,0],[-1,2]]. The passages and the oracle support the finding.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6: history.mdx:67 says 'Donnelly and Eriksson use the game to prove that a connected graph with whole-number road counts is a Dynkin diagram of finite type exactly when some start that has no negative number and is not all zeros gives a game that ends'. 'counts' and 'finite' link to glossary entries. The glossary's 'finite' entry reads 'A connected board with roads both ways is finite ... Every other board is neither', and its 'board' entry allows 'any number of them in each direction'. M3:121 states the same theorem with 'a connected board with roads both ways'. Oracle: board_kind([[2,0],[-1,2]]) = 'one-way'; classify gives [{'nodes':[1,2],'kind':'one-way','balanced':False,'class':None,'name':None}]; play(C,(1,0)) = ((-1,-1), word [0,1], fired [1,1]). In labels that is word 1, 2, and the game ends after 2 moves, as observed. Tried R1 on SPEC 2.1 'Unless stated otherwise a board is bidirected'. It fails: the sentence fixes the specification's own default, while the history sentence says 'graph with whole-number road counts', the site defines one-way boards for its readers (glossary row 2), and 2.1 itself says the theory does not apply to them. The [D] of 2.11 covers only the reading of the Mutation Conjecture. decisions/P6-A6.md ('the history page' and its repair) records no choice about this hypothesis, and no MERGE or known-and-decided item touches it. gate-G6 and earlier rounds have no record of it.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because SPEC 2.1's bidirected default governs the specification's text, not a site sentence about graphs with road counts, and 2.1 excludes one-way boards from the theory. R2 failed, because SOURCES [DE08] and M3 beat 7 restrict the theorem, and the parenthetical about the literature is the lens's gloss but is not needed for the cause. R3 failed, because history.mdx is phase 6. R4 failed, because the oracle confirms the counterexample (classify class None; play from (1,0) ends in 2 moves). R5 failed: there is no [D] or recorded decision. R6 failed: there is no record. The severity stays blocker, since a theorem stated without its hypothesis is false as printed.

verdicts.citation: SPEC 2.14 'Orbit polytopes': 'a polytope whose combinatorics depend only on which nodes are ringed'; and in the same section, 'the integer orbit (0,1,1) has the right combinatorics and edges of two lengths [V]'; 'Edge lengths: ... squared length a_i^2(α_i,α_i)=2d_i a_i^2 [V]'; golden wythoff_note. These support the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6: glossary.mdx:551, row 64: 'Its shape depends only on which nodes are ringed (Cox35, CKPS95).'. P6-A8.json lists it as a statement with that provenance. Oracle with B = gram(cartan('B',3)): wythoff_f_vector gives [24,36,14,1] for both (0,1,1) and (0,2,1). The squared form lengths over wythoff_edges are {2,4} and {2,16}, ratios 2 and 8, as observed. golden wythoff_note: 'edge from lambda to s_i lambda has squared length a_i^2 (alpha_i, alpha_i); uniform needs a_i |alpha_i| constant on ringed nodes'. SPEC uses 'shape' only for tableaux, for 'Special shapes' of Satake diagrams and for M7's question, never as a synonym for combinatorics. The [D] of 2.14 covers only 'make uniform'. The same words appear in M7 beat 2 (phase 4). round-p4/out/RT-09.json noted them as 'Not reported, imprecise wording'. That was a note, not a finding, ruling or decision, so R6 cannot use it. No DECISIONS.md entry addresses the word.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed, because 2.14 says combinatorics and contrasts it with edge lengths. R2 failed, because the finding quotes 2.14 exactly. R3 failed, because row 64 is phase 6 (P6-A8). R4 failed, because the oracle confirms equal f-vectors and unequal edge ratios. R5 failed: the [D] of 2.14 covers make uniform only. R6 failed: the phase 4 note is not a tracked open item. The severity stays minor, since 'shape' admits a combinatorial reading and the rubric's 'wording' fits.

Kac numbers the nodes of E6, E7, E8 and G2 differently ([S2] for E6, [U] for the rest)'; DECISIONS.md 'MERGE: P6-A4 reviewed; rulings; merge checks after T13 and T14', ruling (b); DECISIONS.md 'P6-A4: the convention switch says nothing of Kac's numbering outside E4 (repair after review)'. verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6: m10-atlas.mdx:55, li data-hub-item='atlas': 'with a switch that prints the Cartan matrix as this site, Kac and SageMath write it or as Bourbaki and Humphreys write it, transposed'. Tried R2 and R1: 2.9's translation cell says 'same matrix' for Kac, which could support a convention-only reading. But the same cell goes straight on to say that Kac numbers E6 [S2] and E7, E8, G2 [U] differently. MERGE ruling (b) on P6-A4 held that the legend 'Show the Cartan matrix as it is printed by' with the option 'This site, Kac and SageMath' says outside the E4 wrapper that 'Kac prints this matrix with this numbering' (P6-A4-review.json: 'Together these say Kac prints this exact matrix'). It required the legend 'in the convention of'. The hub's 'prints ... as ... Kac ... write it' is the wording that ruling rejected. decisions/P6-A8.md ('the hub items') claims the sentence 'says nothing of Kac's numbering (E4)'. That is the builder's own reading, and no MERGE ruling confirms it for the hub. MERGE 'P6 stage 6.3' merged P6-A8 without ruling on this sentence. The known-and-decided list holds nothing on it. M10 is phase 6. gate-G6 has no record of it.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 and R2 failed, because 2.9's 'same matrix' is qualified in the same cell by Kac's different numbering, and MERGE ruling (b) read the equivalent legend wording as a claim about Kac's printed matrix. R3 failed, because M10 is phase 6. R4 does not apply, since this is a statement about a source, not an oracle value. R5 failed: P6-A8's self-assessment is not a ruling, and no [D] applies. R6 failed: there is no record. Severity: the rubric does not clearly name a claim about a book's numbering. Minor fits 'wording'. For the owner, the P6-A4 review graded the same wording on the Atlas legend as a major.
